# rediscloud_iris_agent_memory_extractor (Resource)

Manages a direct Iris agent-memory resource, independently of Redis Cloud CAPI.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "rediscloud_iris_agent_memory_extractor" "example" {
  store_id    = rediscloud_iris_agent_memory.example.id
  name        = "document-profile"
  memory_type = rediscloud_iris_agent_memory_type.example.name
  source      = "DOCUMENTS"
  strategy    = "CUSTOM"
  prompt      = "Extract the user's preferences."
  enabled     = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `memory_type` (String) Must be a memory type registered on the store.
- `name` (String) Display name of any API resource.
- `prompt` (String)
- `source` (String)
- `store_id` (String) Server-generated store identifier: st_ followed by 32 lowercase hex characters.
- `strategy` (String)

### Optional

- `destination_namespace_id` (String) Destination namespace identifier. Use an empty string to clear it.
- `enabled` (Boolean)

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `extractor_id` (String) Server-generated extractor identifier: ex_ followed by 32 lowercase hex characters.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier used for import.
- `revision` (String) Resource revision. Opaque: each change to a resource's own configuration writes a
new value, and a resource never gets a value it had before. Compare for equality
only; its format is the service's, so only its length is constrained. Returned as
`revision`; sent back as `expectedRevision` to make a write conditional. Omitting
`expectedRevision` makes the write unconditional.
- `updated_at` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import rediscloud_iris_agent_memory_extractor.example st_11111111111111111111111111111111/ex_22222222222222222222222222222222
```
